title: To Keep the Lamp Alive
description: To Keep the Lamp Alive in Tonic Solfa to BOYLSTON, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 6 verses and a piano.
about: William Cowper wrote these words. They were printed in Olney Hymns (London, 1779), Book III, hymn 74, “Dependance”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Short Metre (6.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to BOYLSTON; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: To keep the lamp a-live With oil we fill the bowl; 'Tis wa-ter makes the wil-low thrive, And grace that feeds the soul.

lines: With oil we fill the bowl;
And grace that feeds the soul.
It is not at our own command,
And e'en an angel would be weak,
This more exalts the King of kings

source: John Newton and William Cowper, Olney Hymns (1779)
licence: Public domain: William Cowper died in 1800.
credits: Words by William Cowper (1731–1800), public domain, as printed in Olney Hymns (1779); set to BOYLSTON by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
